content.title: Steve Kerr explains why Warriors are resting Steph Curry vs. Lakers, not Kings
content.text: Warriors fans haven’t received their usual dose of Steph Curry magic at Chase Center this season, and that trend continued Thursday when Golden State’s star guard was ruled out of the regular-season home finale against the Los Angeles Lakers due to knee injury management. But when a reporter at Steve Kerr’s Thursday pregame press conference asked the Warriors coach if the team had given any thought to letting Curry play in front of his home fans one more time—and resting him Friday in Sacramento instead—Kerr insisted there was nothing to be done. “It was a hundred percent health related,” Kerr said. “If we were making decisions on [those] criteria, we would have played him tonight. But this was 100 percent about his health and recovery from the two games that he’s played and the preparation for next week. This made the most sense.” The Warriors are locked into the No. 10 seed in the Western Conference and, mathematically, have nothing left to play for until the NBA play-in tournament begins. Still, fans were surely looking forward to the latest chapter in the Curry-LeBron James saga, one that now will likely have to wait until next season. The Warriors aren’t taking any chances with Curry, however. The four-time NBA champion missed 27 straight games with a nagging “runner’s knee” injury that turned Golden State’s season upside-down, and now that he has returned, the team’s priority is keeping him on the court when the games matter most. “Steph’s doing well,” Kerr said. “Just with the ramp-up, playing the last two games [and] three in four nights to end the season, it makes the most sense to give him tonight…he’ll be good to go [Friday] night.” The Warriors will play either the Portland Trail Blazers or the Los Angeles Clippers on the road in the first round of the play-in tournament next Wednesday.
